context: Remote Locations: The equipment shall recharge the system in remote locations without support from electrical utility infrastructure. Use of Infrastructure: The equipment shall use electrical utility infrastructure when it is available.

Shock Exposure: When upgraded to transport astronaut, shock accelerations resulting from traversing a single bump at 15 km/h shall not exceed 2.5 g (measured on the floor at the occupant's feet.) This requirement shall be satisfied by the Lunar Exploration Light Rover throughout its operating weight range.

ASP shall provide a search capability (Query) which can perform a full-text search by keyword across the filesystem. Each application in the ASP shall provide a search capability which can perform a keyword search within its database.

ASP shall provide a disaster management tool which enables users to Put/Get data, including the ability to upload and view data about volunteers, upload, search and view data on missing people. ASP shall provide a suite of applications which can expose lists of major entities in their data models to external applications via XML-based feeds (e.g., RSS, GeoRSS) and/or XMl-based APIs (e.g., REST).

Hardware shall offer the interfaces specified in 3.2.4.1 and shall support the addition of external hardware devices, networking devices, and graphic devices via these interfaces. Hardware shall be built to maximize its durability in the austere conditions of the field, balanced with simplicity and affordability.
Hardware shall not be expected to offer hardware-level security. VM Client Software shall be selected based on its ability to meet the specifications in 3.2.2.

A ventricular sense is deemed to be a premature ventricular contraction if there has been no atrial event since the previous ventricular event. Atrial or ventricular markers may have modifiers that change their meaning.

When Extended PVARP is enabled, an occurrence of a premature ventricular contraction (PVC) shall cause the pulse generator to use the Extended PVARP value for the post-ventricular atrial refractory period following the PVC. The PVARP shall always return to its normal programmed value on the subsequent cardiac cycle regardless of PVC and other events.
